passage.zh: 咖啡廳內坐著來自四面八方的人，像是等待外帶的上班族、安靜閱讀書報的學生，或是與三五好友一起聊天的老人家。

passage.en: The café is full of people from all over: office workers waiting for takeaway, students quietly reading books and newspapers, or old people chatting with a few friends.

passage.zh: 而我，通常選擇靠近窗戶的角落坐下來，在喝咖啡的同時，也觀察窗外人們的一舉一動，這是我最享受的休閒時光。
passage.py: Ér wǒ, tōngcháng xuǎnzé kàojìn chuānghù de jiǎoluò zuòxià lái, zài Hēkāfēi de tóngshí, yě guānchá chuāngwài rénmen de yìjǔyídòng, zhè shì wǒ zuì xiǎngshòu de xiūxián shíguāng.
passage.en: As for me, I usually sit in a corner by the window, and while drinking coffee I watch every move of the people outside. This is the leisure time I enjoy most.

The latest research shows that health supplements have no effect on brain aging, and always doing the same things will also limit the brain's development.

passage.en: A survey on adults' preferred study times shows that most adults think night is the best time to study, with 40% to 60% agreeing;

passage.zh: 其次是上午時段，多受不靠勞力工作的人所喜愛，如在學青年和退休人士。
passage.py: Qícì shì shàngwǔ shíduàn, duō shòu búkào láolì gōngzuò de rén suǒ xǐài, rúzài xué qīngnián hé tuìxiū rénshì.
passage.en: next is the morning, preferred mostly by people who don't do physical work, such as young people in school and retirees.

passage.zh: 另外，在一週之中，週末被認為最不適合學習，原因在於成年人大多希望利用週末從事家庭休閒活動。
passage.py: Lìngwài, zài yìzhōu zhīzhōng, zhōumò bèi rènwéi zuì bù shìhé xuéxí, yuányīn zàiyú chéngniánrén dàduō xīwàng lìyòng zhōumò cóngshì jiātíng xiūxiánhuódòng.
passage.en: In addition, within the week, weekends are considered the least suitable time to study, because most adults want to use weekends for family leisure activities.

passage.zh: 成人教育課程的時間規劃正可由此得到啟發，比起過去一直被廣泛討論與強調的學習技巧，如果轉為綜合考察成年學習者的學習慣例，進行課程的安排與調整，肯定能達到更好的學習效果。
passage.py: Chéngrénjiàoyù kèchéng de shíjiān guīhuà zhèng kě yóucǐ dédào qǐfā, bǐqǐ guòqù yìzhí bèi guǎngfàn tǎolùn yǔ qiángdiào de xuéxí jìqiǎo, rúguǒ zhuǎnwéi zōnghé kǎochá chéngnián xuéxízhě de xuéxí guànlì, jìnxíng kèchéng de ānpái yǔ tiáozhěng, kěndìng néng dádào gènghǎo de xuéxíxiàoguǒ.
passage.en: This can inspire how adult education courses are scheduled: rather than the study techniques that have long been widely discussed and emphasized, if courses were arranged and adjusted by looking comprehensively at adult learners' study habits, better learning results would certainly be achieved.

passage.py: Gèfāng wèi néng gòumǎi jūnshì wǔqì, fēifǎ qǔdé yǔ fànmài zuànshí yǐ zhuànqǔ dàliàng jīnqián, dǎozhì gèfāng yīnwèi zhēngqiǎng zuànshí láiyuán, yòu fādòng wúshùcì de dàxiǎo zhànzhēng, zàochéng shùshíwàn rén sǐwáng, xiānxuè rǎnhóng le tǔdì, zhèxiē shǎnshǎnfāguāng de “Zuànshí”, yòu bèi chēngwéi “Xuè zuànshí”.
passage.en: To buy weapons, the various sides illegally obtained and sold diamonds to earn large amounts of money. Fighting over diamond sources, they then launched countless wars large and small, causing hundreds of thousands of deaths and staining the land red with blood. These sparkling "diamonds" are also called "blood diamonds."

passage.zh: 正因為有人願意買鑽石，以此滿足自己，就有人會為了挖鑽石而付出生命。
passage.py: Zhèng yīnwèi yǒurén yuànyì mǎi zuànshí, yǐcǐ mǎnzú zìjǐ, jiù yǒurén huì wèile wā zuànshí ér fùchū shēngmìng.
passage.en: Precisely because some people are willing to buy diamonds to satisfy themselves, others will give their lives to dig for them.

passage.zh: 為了一個浪漫的理由，卻間接助長了戰爭。
passage.py: Wèile yí ge làngmàn de lǐyóu, què jiànjiē zhùzhǎng le zhànzhēng.
passage.en: For a romantic reason, people indirectly fuel war.

passage.zh: 當我們知道「血鑽石」背後的歷史後，怎麼還能不論代價，把它戴在身上呢？
passage.py: Dāng wǒmen zhīdào “Xuè zuànshí” bèihòu de lìshǐ hòu, zěnme hái néng búlùn dàijià, bǎ tā dài zài shēnshàng ne?

passage.en: Three young people learning to paint planned to sell their works for NT$1,000 each. Their customers all said the same thing: "I'm afraid your painting isn't worth NT$1,000, is it?"

passage.zh: 其中一人聽了以後，仔細看了看自己的畫，最後不但以兩千元賣掉畫，還更加努力成為著名的畫家。
passage.py: Qízhōng yī rén tīng le yǐhòu, zǐxì kàn le kàn zìjǐ de huà, zuìhòu búdàn yǐ liǎngqiānyuán màidiào huà, hái gèngjiā nǔlì chéngwéi zhùmíng de huàjiā.
passage.en: One of them, on hearing this, looked carefully at his painting; in the end he not only sold it for NT$2,000, but worked even harder and became a famous painter.

passage.zh: 另一人聽了以後只是把畫撕了，從此不畫了，他努力學習攝影而成為有名的攝影大師。

passage.en: Another, on hearing it, just tore up his painting and stopped painting from then on; he worked hard at learning photography and became a famous master photographer.

passage.zh: 第三人以為自己的畫真的不夠好，就降價以五百元賣出。

passage.zh: 最後他為了生活，只能在路邊賣些沒有價值的便宜畫作。
passage.py: Zuìhòu tā wèile shēnghuó, zhǐnéng zài lùbiān mài xiē méiyǒu jiàzhí de piányi huàzuò.
passage.en: In the end, to make a living, he could only sell cheap, worthless paintings by the roadside.

passage.zh: 批評有正面的鼓勵效果，可以讓人繼續努力往前走，或是指引你走向另一條成功的路；
passage.py: Pīpíng yǒu zhèngmiàn de gǔlì xiàoguǒ, kěyǐ ràng rén jìxù nǔlì wǎngqiánzǒu, huòshì zhǐyǐn nǐ zǒuxiàng lìng yìtiáo chénggōng de lù;
passage.en: Criticism can have a positive, encouraging effect—it can make people keep working hard and moving forward, or point you toward another road to success;

passage.zh: 但它有時候是毒藥，會誤了別人一生。
passage.py: Dàn tā yǒushíhòu shì dúyào, huì wù le biérén yìshēng.
passage.en: but sometimes it is poison and can ruin someone's whole life.

passage.zh: 其實人的一生會遇到無數的批評，但自己的人生自己決定，在面對批評時反省與思考，就有機會使毒藥成為解藥。
passage.py: Qíshí rén de yìshēng huì yùdào wúshù de pīpíng, dàn zìjǐ de rénshēng zìjǐ juédìng, zài miànduì pīpíng shí fǎnxǐng yǔ sīkǎo, jiù yǒu jīhuì shǐ dúyào chéngwéi jiěyào.
passage.en: In fact, people meet countless criticisms in their lives, but your life is yours to decide. If you reflect and think when facing criticism, you have a chance to turn poison into antidote.

passage.py: (Shí)

passage.zh: 你聽過「熱狗水」嗎？
passage.py: Nǐ tīng guò “Règǒu shuǐ” ma?
passage.en: Have you heard of "hot dog water"?

passage.zh: 如果有人告訴你，它可以讓你減輕體重、增加活力，價格是一般飲料的二十倍，你買不買？
passage.py: Rúguǒ yǒurén gàosù nǐ, tā kěyǐ ràng nǐ jiǎnqīng tǐzhòng, zēngjiā huólì, jiàgé shì yìbān yǐnliào de èrshíbèi, nǐ mǎi bù mǎi?
passage.en: If someone told you it could help you lose weight and boost your energy, and it cost twenty times as much as an ordinary drink, would you buy it?

passage.zh: 在溫哥華上週的無車日活動上，就擺了一個賣熱狗水的攤子，雖然商品說明聽起來很吸引人，可是誰都看得出來，它就是一瓶水裡面泡著一條熱狗而已，最後卻仍在活動當天賣出了六十瓶。
passage.py: Zài Wēngēhuá shàngzhōu de wúchērì huódòng shàng, jiù bǎi le yí ge mài règǒu shuǐ de tānzi, suīrán shāngpǐn shuōmíng tīng qǐlái hěn xīyǐn rén, kěshì shuí dōu kàndéchūlái, tā jiùshì yìpíng shuǐ lǐmiàn pàozhù yìtiáo règǒu éryǐ, zuìhòu què réng zài huódòng dàngtiān màichū le liùshí píng.
passage.en: At last week's car-free day event in Vancouver there was a stall selling hot dog water. Although the product description sounded attractive, anyone could see it was just a bottle of water with a hot dog soaking in it—yet sixty bottles were sold on the day.

passage.zh: 那些人在掏出錢包之前，一定都沒有仔細閱讀瓶子包裝上面的小字：「熱狗水是希望鼓勵大家批判思考，並意識到自己的消費行為究竟是受何種因素左右。」
passage.py: Nàxiē rén zài tāochū qiánbāo zhīqián, yídìng dōu méiyǒu zǐxìyuèdú píngzi bāozhuāng shàngmiàn de xiǎozì: “Règǒu shuǐ shì xīwàng gǔlì dàjiā pīpàn sīkǎo, bìng yìshí dào zìjǐ de xiāofèixíngwéi jiūjìng shì shòu hézhǒng yīnsù zuǒyòu.”
passage.en: Before taking out their wallets, those people surely hadn't read the small print on the bottle's packaging: "Hot dog water hopes to encourage everyone to think critically and become aware of what factors actually influence their consumer behavior."

passage.zh: 原來這是一個行為實驗，目的是觀察人們是否會相信這樣誇張的商品。
passage.py: Yuánlái zhè shì yí ge xíngwéi shíyàn, mùdì shì guānchá rénmen shìfǒu huì xiāngxìn zhèyàng kuāzhāng de shāngpǐn.
passage.en: It turned out to be a behavioral experiment, aimed at seeing whether people would believe in such an exaggerated product.

passage.zh: 受騙的人買到教訓了嗎？
passage.py: Shòupiàn de rén mǎidào jiàoxùn le ma?
passage.en: Did the people who were fooled learn their lesson?

passage.zh: 那得看他們是否知道自己上當了，即使知道，恐怕也不保證他們下一次不會再度賠上冤枉錢。
passage.py: Nà dé kàn tāmen shìfǒu zhīdào zìjǐ shàngdàng le, jíshǐ zhīdào, kǒngpà yě bù bǎozhèng tāmen xià yícì búhuì zàidù péi shàng yuānwǎngqián.
passage.en: That depends on whether they know they were tricked. Even if they know, there's probably no guarantee they won't waste their money again next time.

passage.zh: （十二）
passage.py: (Shíèr)

passage.zh: 在某些社會文化中，由於「一個人吃飯」通常與被孤立、沒朋友、不懂社交等負面印象聯繫在一起，所以一個人走進餐廳就成了許多人害怕的事。
passage.py: Zài mǒuxiē shèhuì wénhuà zhōng, yóuyú “Yí ge rén chīfàn” tōngcháng yǔ bèi gūlì, méi péngyǒu, bù dǒng shèjiāo děng fùmiàn yìnxiàng liánxì zài yìqǐ, suǒyǐ yí ge rén zǒujìn cāntīng jiù chéng le xǔduō rén hàipà de shì.
passage.en: In some social cultures, because "eating alone" is usually associated with negative impressions such as being isolated, having no friends or lacking social skills, walking into a restaurant alone has become something many people fear.

passage.zh: 但，獨自吃飯真是一件那麼糟糕的事嗎？
passage.py: Dàn, dúzì chīfàn zhēnshì yíjiàn nàme zāogāo de shì ma?
passage.en: But is eating alone really such a terrible thing?

passage.zh: 事實上，一個人並不意味著寂寞，與此相反，更可以將注意力放在享受餐盤上的美食。
passage.py: Shìshíshàng, yí ge rén bìng bù yìwèizhù jìmò, yǔcǐxiāngfǎn, gèng kěyǐ jiāng zhùyìlì fàngzài xiǎngshòu cānpán shàng de měishí.
passage.en: In fact, being alone doesn't mean being lonely; on the contrary, you can focus more on enjoying the food on your plate.

passage.zh: 當然，與他人分享、交流時能帶給人們滿足與快樂，而當你已經在人際相處上付出了許多時間後，更應該為自己保留一些獨處的空間；
passage.py: Dāngrán, yǔ tārén fēnxiǎng, jiāoliú shínéng dàigěi rénmen mǎnzú yǔ kuàilè, érdāng nǐ yǐjīng zài rénjì xiāngchǔ shàng fùchū le xǔduō shíjiān hòu, gèng yīnggāi wèi zìjǐ bǎoliú yìxiē dúchǔ de kōngjiān;
passage.en: Of course, sharing and interacting with others can bring people satisfaction and happiness, and when you've already spent a lot of time on relationships, you should keep some space to be alone for yourself;

passage.zh: 當你因為獨自吃飯而害怕被貼上「人際障礙」的標籤時，也許根本沒有人注意到你，或是覺得你性格古怪。
passage.py: Dāng nǐ yīnwèi dúzì chīfàn ér hàipà bèi tiē shàng “Rénjì zhàngài” de biāoqiān shí, yěxǔ gēnběn méiyǒu rén zhùyì dào nǐ, huòshì juéde nǐ xìnggé gǔguài.
passage.en: when you fear being labeled as having "social difficulties" because you eat alone, perhaps nobody even notices you or thinks you're odd.

passage.zh: 忙碌的生活常常讓我們忽略與自己獨處的重要性，哪怕是一頓飯、一部電影的時間，都是面對自己的好機會。
passage.py: Mánglù de shēnghuó chángcháng ràng wǒmen hūlüè yǔ zìjǐ dúchǔ de zhòngyàoxìng, nǎpà shì yídùnfàn, yíbù diànyǐng de shíjiān, dōu shì miànduì zìjǐ de hǎo jīhuì.
passage.en: Busy lives often make us overlook the importance of being alone with ourselves; even the time of one meal or one movie is a good chance to face yourself.

passage.zh: 久而久之，你將發現，那些異樣眼光只是一種自我限制，而能一個人吃飯，竟然是那麼寶貴。
passage.py: Jiǔérjiǔzhī, nǐ jiāng fāxiàn, nàxiē yìyàng yǎnguāng zhǐshì yìzhǒng zìwǒ xiànzhì, ér néng yí ge rén chīfàn, jìngrán shì nàme Bǎoguì.
passage.en: Over time you'll find that those strange looks are just a self-imposed limit, and being able to eat alone is actually so precious.

stem.zh: 作者認為有些人害怕一個人吃飯的原因是什麼？
stem.py: Zuòzhě rènwéi yǒuxiē rén hàipà yí ge rén chīfàn de yuányīn shì shénme?
stem.en: Why does the author think some people are afraid to eat alone?
